kicker: The garden has a gate — who holds the key?
summary: AI is not just technology — it is a matter of power and of the choices a society makes.

options: Everything is public, including the training data
You can download what it has learned and run or fine-tune it yourself
Anyone can edit the model on the company's servers
You may use it however you like, no licence needed
quiz.explain: Open weights means the trained “brain” can be downloaded. The training data usually is not included, and a licence still sets how you may use it.

gate.label: Walled garden, open garden
gate.art: Two gardens under one moon: one behind a whitewashed wall with only a small window where you ask for a branch at a time; one with its bamboo gate wide open, where anyone can dig up a plant and grow it at home. Lanterns hang at both gates.
gate.toggleAria: Switch between the walled garden and the open garden
gate.tradeoffLabel: What you gain, what you give up

tradeoffs.name: Freedom
tradeoffs.closed: You play by the company's rules; you cannot change the inside.
tradeoffs.open: Download it, fine-tune it, run it wherever you like.

tradeoffs.name: Cost
tradeoffs.closed: Pay per use or by plan; no powerful computer needed.
tradeoffs.open: No per-use fees, but you supply the hardware, power and upkeep.

tradeoffs.name: Privacy
tradeoffs.closed: Your data passes through the company's servers.
tradeoffs.open: Run it on your own machine and your data never leaves it.

tradeoffs.name: Risk of misuse
tradeoffs.closed: The company can block harmful requests and close abusive accounts.
tradeoffs.open: Once released it cannot be recalled; others can strip out its safety guards.

insight.text: An open-weight model lets you download its trained “brain”; a closed model can only be used through an app or API.

detail.text: Example: in Aug 2025 OpenAI released gpt-oss with open weights under Apache 2.0; it says the small version runs in 16 GB of memory.

gate.caveat: Open weights is not fully open source: the data and training method are usually not published. See station 31 for where to download models.

fence.label: Fenced-off models
fence.art: In the middle of the garden is a small plot fenced with bamboo and thorny rope; only wall guards carrying stamped lanterns may step inside. Within, a very bright lamp lights up every crack in the city wall outside.
fence.gateAria: Try the fence gate: see who gets in and why
fence.denied: The gate opens only for vetted wall guards.

fact.text: Apr 2026: Anthropic gave Mythos Preview only to organisations that find and fix software flaws (Project Glasswing), with no plan for wide release.
Sep 2026: Google set up its Fairwind programme, giving its strongest cybersecurity model only to vetted defenders.

why.text: Anthropic says this model finds and exploits flaws better than most experts; a wide release would hand it to attackers too.

debate.text: Who decides who gets inside the fence, and who independently checks the abilities the companies claim for themselves?

insight.text: In 2026 both Anthropic and Google kept their strongest cybersecurity models fenced off: vetted defenders go first.

fence.detail: Look back at station 19: the fenced summit. Here we ask the next question: who holds the key to the gate?

laws.label: The tide of law
laws.art: A long strip of sand unrolled like an ancient law scroll under the moon; as the moon passes, a carved stone pillar rises from the sand. At the far end, the pillar bearing Vietnam's name is still wet from the tide, its carving not yet dry.
laws.prompt: Drag the moon through the laws
laws.sliderAria: Drag the moon through the AI-law milestones

milestones.label: EU: the AI Act takes effect

fact.text: The EU AI Act takes effect, phased in according to the risk level of each kind of application.
EU bans start to apply to AI uses with unacceptable risk, such as social scoring.
China requires AI-generated content to be labelled: a visible label and a hidden one in the file's data.
The National Assembly passes the Artificial Intelligence Law: 35 articles, risk-based rules, in force from 1 March 2026.

milestones.label: US: an order on state laws

fact.text: The US President signs an order creating a federal legal task force to challenge state AI laws seen as obstructive.
Decree 142/2026 takes effect: AI is split into three risk levels, and AI-made images, audio and video must carry an identifying mark.
The EU amends the law (the Omnibus package): high-risk AI rules move to 2 Dec 2027, and AI built into products to 2 Aug 2028.
According to a June 2026 analysis, Vietnam's list of high-risk AI systems was still awaiting the Prime Minister's sign-off.

horizon.text: AI laws will keep being rewritten as the technology changes; today's deadline may not be tomorrow's.

insight.text: Each its own path: the EU regulates by risk, China requires labels, Vietnam has its own new law, the US still argues.

copyright.label: Copyright & training data
copyright.art: Five stones round a moon lake; the water reflects thousands of pages, paintings and songs. A bucket is drawn from the lake — the training data — and each stone sees that bucket differently.

view.text: Tens of thousands of artists and writers signed a statement (Oct 2024): training AI on work without permission is an unjust threat.
OpenAI (Jan 2024): training on publicly available internet material is “fair use”, though it still lets content owners opt out.
June 2025, a US judge: training on lawfully bought books is fair use; downloading pirated books to build a library is not.
The EU requires general-purpose model providers to have a copyright policy and publish a summary of the data used for training.
US Copyright Office (Jan 2025): typing a prompt alone does not make you an author; purely AI-made material is not protected.

common.text: Everyone agrees training data has value; they differ on whether its makers must be asked and paid.

cases.text: Jul 2026: a US court gave final approval to Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement with authors, about $3,000 per book.
Sep 2026: a US appeals court upheld the ruling that Ross copying Westlaw's legal notes to train AI was not fair use.

insight.text: Copyright over training data is unsettled: courts and lawmakers are still redrawing the lines, each in their own way.
